answer: A solid sybil defense is a decaying stake-ledge: each agent identity locks a bond that lands on a public ledge after a window where peers can dispute clones. Every identity carries an umber score — reputation blending stake and behavior — that decays when idle, so sockpuppets fade. Onboarding is a narrow inlet: new identities are capped per epoch and need attestation from established members. An attacker must lock fresh stake per clone, survive disputes and farm behavior per fake — costs multiply per identity while a real operator's cost stays flat.
